free_tier.stated: 'unlimited storage' per Mapillary's own blog: 'Mapillary offers unlimited storage and makes imagery publicly available ... any organization, public or private, can store and host their archive of street-level imagery at no cost.' No published per-account byte cap. 2.4 billion images hosted.

egress.terms: Free for all use, including commercial, since the Meta acquisition (2020). But API reads are rate-limited, not byte-metered.

record.interface_detail: Graph API at graph.mapillary.com (images, map features, detections); upload via mapillary_tools CLI or Desktop Uploader
record.tooling: `mapillary_tools` (pip), Mapillary Desktop Uploader, official Python SDK, MapillaryJS
record.chaining: Writes are geographically anchored, so this is a corpus, not a bucket. Read path returns tile/thumb URLs; a normal CDN in front works, but origin fetch is token-gated.
record.limits_note: per-image: 200 MP resolution ceiling, landscape orientation, EXIF GPS + timestamp required. Read side: graph.mapillary.com 50,000 requests/minute/app; tiles.mapillary.com 50,000 requests/DAY. The forum thread 'Can and does someone replicate the Mapillary images database?' states outright that the free plan's 50,000-image limit blocks bulk re-download.

identity_cost.detail: Email. Confirmed: graph.mapillary.com with no token returns {"message":"Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token","code":190}, and signup is a Meta/Facebook or email account with a free developer token; no affiliation check. help.mapillary.com article 'An Introduction to Mapillary' says 'All you need to start contributing is your smartphone and our mobile app.'.

record.reliability_note: Uploads are unmetered, while bulk retrieval is rate-limited to 50,000 vector tile requests per day via API.
